channel.title: AI Trend Analysis Reports
channel.description: Cross-checked analysis of technology, industry and market trends

item.title: There Was No Protocol War — How MCP and A2A Divided the Layers
item.description: MCP joined the Linux Foundation in December 2025 and A2A in August 2026, ending the standards race as a division of layers. MCP passed 400M monthly downloads; A2A passed 150 organizations. The remaining gap is authorization and audit.

item.title: The Bar a Shelved Model Left Behind — What the GPT-6.1 Astra Cancellation Revealed
item.description: OpenAI shelved GPT-6.1 Astra over safety findings and released GPT-6.1 Sol the next day, matching Astra on DeepSWE v1.1 at one-fifth the token price. The release bar is no longer capability but staying within authorization.

item.title: Where Decision Models Sit in AI Research, and Where Their Roots Are
item.description: Jev and Laya are not a new discipline but the latest point in discriminative classification: calibration traces to Brier (1950) and accept/escalate to Chow's 1957 reject option. The novelty sits in the interface, not the science.

item.title: Decision Models: Jev, Laya, and the Three Weeks of System One
item.description: "System One models" that return a verdict instead of prose became a category in three weeks, with 25-plus open clones. Yet in the first independent benchmark a 2023 DeBERTa classifier beat Jev at 89.01% / 54ms versus 86.35% / 348ms.

item.title: AI Career Guidance Platforms: From Self-Report to Verified Evidence
item.description: LinkedIn replaced self-reported badges with Verified AI Skill Levels in January 2026, moving the contest from algorithms to data provenance. The market compounds at 22% toward $14.8B by 2030. Google Career Dreamer, LinkedIn, Teal and Gloat compared across four tiers.

item.title: The Technical Evolution of Task-Oriented Dialogue
item.description: Dialogue state tracking moved to function calling, letting 7B models surpass the prior state of the art by 5.6pp. Evaluation is shifting too, from turn accuracy to trajectory completion via τ-bench.

item.title: Task-Oriented Dialogue Systems: A Deep Analysis
item.description: A forty-year-old four-component design is the standard again in the LLM era, and capital is concentrating on support agents: Sierra at $15.8B, Decagon at $4.5B. Yet against 66% adoption, only 23% report meaningful ROI.

item.title: OpenMAIC, Examined: Tsinghua's Multi-Agent AI Classroom
item.description: Tsinghua's OpenMAIC drew 39,290 stars in six months and generates the class itself, not study material. But the paper's lowest satisfaction item is 3.51/5, and versions up to 1.0.0 carried an unauthenticated SSRF flaw.

item.title: Half the Fortune 500 on Open-Source AI? What the Number Measures
item.description: Hugging Face says half the Fortune 500 uses open-source AI, yet open source's share of enterprise LLM usage fell from 19% to 11%. We explain why both numbers are true, and what Nvidia's acquisition of Hugging Face changed.

item.title: Sakana AI Deep Dive: 100,000 Companies and "Japan-Spec AI"
item.description: Sakana AI partnered with Sumitomo Corporation and SCSK to push domestic AI through a 100,000-company network. We map its $2.7B valuation and its finance and defense contracts, and test the limits of performance figures that are all self-reported.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra and the Global AGI Race
item.description: OpenAI declared the "AGI era" while shipping GPT-6 Astra in a restricted form, and Anthropic sells one model in two safeguard tiers; frontier pricing converged at $10/$50 as Chinese open weights closed to within 2.7 points of the best U.S. model.

item.title: MoAI-ADK and Spec-Driven Development: The Return of TDD and DDD
item.description: As trust in AI coding fell from 40% to 29%, spec-driven development went mainstream in 2026; graph-based impact analysis cut test regression from 6.08% to 1.82%.

item.title: Purpose-Built Recommendation Chatbots: Methodology and Market
item.description: Eval-driven development is now standard, yet a measured 0.15 shift from merely swapping the judge model shows the ruler itself needs calibrating; the conversational systems market reaches $32.2B in 2026.

item.title: AIO and SEO Global Trends, and Lighthouse
item.description: Zero-click searches hit 68% as the success metric shifts from clicks to citations; with major AI crawlers not rendering JavaScript, Lighthouse 13 and SSR became preconditions for AI visibility.

item.title: The EU AI Act for Open Badge Issuers: A Regulatory Deep Dive
item.description: High-risk obligations apply in full from August 2026: issuing badges on AI auto-grading is high-risk "learning-outcome evaluation," and emotion recognition is prohibited (up to 7% of turnover). An activity-by-activity risk table sets response priorities.

item.title: Evelyn Voice Tutor Deep Dive: Product, Technology, Business, Key People
item.description: Dissecting a 24/7 AI tutor that syncs voice conversation with a whiteboard: a content firm founded in 2013 bootstrapped its way into AI products and ranked No. 9 in the US on TIME's 2026 Top EdTech list.

item.title: Seven AI Career Pathway Services: In-Depth Analysis
item.description: Seven services — Evelyn, Pathly, SkillSeek, Salesforce Career Connect, Google Career Dreamer, LinkedIn Next Role — analyzed in a 10-item feature comparison matrix; with internal mobility up 6%, the battleground is shifting to internal marketplaces.

item.title: 1EdTech TrustEd Credential Coalition: Metadata Requirements In-Depth Analysis
item.description: A credential may carry the "TrustEd" name only if all 8 required metadata fields are met — miss one and it's forfeited. We dissect the quality bar built on OB 3.0 and the OBEE extensions, per the framework finalized in May 2026.

item.title: 1EdTech Trusted Portable Learning Context (TPLC): In-Depth Analysis
item.description: Dissecting the TPLC RFC published by 1EdTech Labs in July 2026: six properties (consent, sovereignty, provenance) for safely delivering a "specific learning moment" to AI agents, plus a new tplc service layer with MCP as transport.

item.title: 1EdTech 2026: Major News & Trends Comprehensive Analysis
item.description: 1EdTech split into Global (public good) and Consortium (standards) entities in June 2026; France's interoperability decree and mass adoption of Open Badges 3.0/CLR 2.0 are turning standards compliance into a procurement requirement.

item.title: Graph RAG Global Trends and Enterprise Adoption
item.description: LazyGraphRAG cuts indexing costs to 0.1% of full GraphRAG, reigniting adoption; LinkedIn proved a 77.6% retrieval accuracy gain in production as the knowledge graph market grows 31.6% annually toward $9.88B by 2032.

item.title: AI Agent Management & Orchestration Platforms: Global Trends
item.description: The AI agent platform market grows to $52.62B by 2030 (46.3% CAGR); Dify raises $30M with 280+ enterprises, becoming the de facto OSS standard. A four-tier analysis of Dify, n8n, Coze, LangGraph, Bedrock AgentCore, and Vertex, plus MCP/A2A and observability standards.

item.title: Personalized AI Agents: Global Trends & Japan-Korea Business Model Deep Dive
item.description: Global AI agent market grows to $182.97B by 2033 (49.6% CAGR); memory becomes default in ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini, while Rakuten AI, Naver Agent N, and Kakao Kanana drive super-app integration and SoftBank-OpenAI Cristal Intelligence leads enterprise deployment in Japan.

item.title: AI Customer Acquisition Services: Global Trends & Japan-Korea Business Models
item.description: Global AI customer acquisition market grows to $47.82B by 2030 (25.8% CAGR); agentic marketing and LLMO emerge as new currents, with LINE-based Saloriza/CAT.AI in Japan and Kakao/Naver-based Search Doogam/Zentoo in Korea leading vertical SaaS expansion.

item.title: The Competency Graph: Global Research and Market Trends
item.description: Research and commercial trends in knowledge graphs linking occupations, skills, and credentials. Talent intelligence software projected at $27.8B by 2033 (~12% CAGR); covers ESCO/O*NET standards, GNN recommenders, and the open B2C gap.

item.title: HyperNova 60B 2605 Deep Dive: CompactifAI Quantum-Inspired Compression
item.description: Multiverse Computing halves OpenAI's gpt-oss-120b: weights drop 121.54GB→31.81GB with ~69% less memory and +36% throughput, while LiveCodeBench (68.68) beats the original.

item.title: 1EdTech AI Content Best Practices v1.0: Document Deep Dive
item.description: A focused dissection of v1.0's five core components: principles, recommendations, five-tier labels, risk tiers, content categories — with a three-axis operational matrix.

item.title: 1EdTech AI-Generated Content Best Practices v1.0: In-Depth Analysis
item.description: Analysis of the December 2025 EdTech GenAI governance standard: five-tier transparency labels, risk-based oversight, QTI/CC/LTI/Caliper integration, and EU AI Act Article 50 alignment.

item.title: Dify Deep Analysis: Open-Source LLMOps and Global Best Practices
item.description: Dify tops open-source LLMOps with 131K+ GitHub stars, 1.4M machines, 280+ enterprises, and $30M Series Pre-A funding; Maersk and Novartis case studies included.

item.title: Japan's Digital Textbooks: Adoption Status and Policy Perspectives
item.description: MEXT plans to formalize digital textbooks as official "textbooks" from 2030. Analysis of the paper/digital/hybrid three-option system and GIGA School Phase 2 status.

item.title: ByteDance Deep Analysis: Global Business Strategy and Tokyo Office
item.description: Surpassing Meta with $155B revenue to become the world's largest social media company. Analysis of Doubao 2.0 AI agent strategy, TikTok US JV, Volcengine's 49% cloud share, and Samsung AI chip collaboration.

item.title: Seedance 2.0: ByteDance's AI Video Generation Revolution and Market Competition
item.description: ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 claims #1 on AI video leaderboards with 4-modality input and native audio co-generation. Competitive analysis with Kling 3.0, Sora 2, and Veo 3.1.

item.title: Video Generation AI Models and E-Learning Course Creation Innovation
item.description: From Sora 2, Veo 3, and Kling 2.6 to local lightweight models like Wan 2.1 and LTX-Video — AI video generation strategies for e-learning with BSH, Xerox, and other global case studies.

item.title: sLLM Development Process: Comprehensive Analysis of Approaches and Global Case Studies
item.description: From synthetic data pretraining to knowledge distillation, QLoRA, and GGUF quantization — a comprehensive analysis of sLLM development with Phi-4, Gemma 3, and Llama 3.2 case studies.

item.title: Harness Engineering: The Critical Infrastructure for Production-Ready AI Agents
item.description: The evolution from Prompt to Context to Harness Engineering is complete. With 57.3% of organizations running agents in production, the AI orchestration market surges toward $30B+.

item.title: AI Learning Content Generation Services: Global Trends and Major Platform Analysis
item.description: As the AI education market grows to $32.27B by 2030, a comprehensive 4-tier analysis of 16 platforms spanning AI course builders, video generators, and enterprise LMS content creation.

item.title: 1EdTech CASE & CLR: Global Best Practices and Use Case Analysis
item.description: The CASE 1.1, CLR 2.0, and Open Badges 3.0 trinity matures as education-employment infrastructure. All 50 U.S. state K-12 standards published, expanding to 30+ countries.

item.title: E-Learning Video Streaming: Technology and Infrastructure Landscape
item.description: As the cloud video streaming market grows to $12.7B by 2034, a comprehensive analysis of core infrastructure technologies — ABR, WebRTC, AI optimization, and DRM — powering educational video delivery.

item.title: Open-Source Multimodal AI Models: Specialized Model Guide & Best Practices
item.description: Comprehensive comparison of open-source models rivaling proprietary offerings across vision-language, image, video, and speech — including Qwen3-VL, FLUX.2, Wan 2.2, and Fish Audio S2.

item.title: Global AI Models & AI Trend Analysis: The Four-Way Frontier Race and the Age of Agentic AI
item.description: Four-way frontier race established with GPT-5.4, Claude Opus 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Grok 4.20. AI agent market expands to $12B as 40% of enterprises adopt agents.

item.title: Schoo vs NetLearning: In-Depth Comparison of Japan's Two Online Learning Giants
item.description: Multi-dimensional comparison of listed startup Schoo (¥2.7B revenue, 0.04% churn) and established NetLearning (7,500 clients, 112M cumulative learners) across strategy, AI, and Open Badges.

item.title: AI Course & Content Auto-Generation Services: Global Platform Analysis and Technical Foundations
item.description: Comparative analysis of 10 major platforms including Coursebox, Synthesia, and Articulate. Technical deep-dive into LLM, RAG, and diffusion model applications for education content generation in a $41B market (CAGR 42.83%).

item.title: Japan's EdTech Industry: The Complete Picture — From K-12 to Corporate Training
item.description: Comprehensive analysis of Japan's EdTech market ($17.7B to $85.4B) across K-12, higher education, corporate training, and lifelong learning. Detailed coverage of AI, cloud, and XR infrastructure transformation.

item.title: Japan EdTech Market Trends: AI and Cloud Adoption at the Forefront
item.description: ChromeOS captures 60% share in GIGA School Phase 2. Japan's "AI Big Three" (atama+, Study Sapuri, Qubena) transform the education market. EdTech market projected to reach $85.4B by 2034.

item.title: Global Learning SLM Trends — In-Depth Analysis
item.description: 5 key trends where SLMs transform education. Phi-4 scores 84.8% on MATH, Gemma 3n supports 140+ languages with multimodal input, SLM market projected to reach $20.7B by 2030.

item.title: SLM In-Depth Analysis for K-12 Education and HR: Gemma 3n / Phi-4 Mini vs SmolLM3 / Llama 3.2 3B
item.description: Domain-optimized SLM comparison: Gemma 3n (2GB RAM multimodal) and Phi-4 Mini (textbook-quality training) for K-12 education vs SmolLM3 (best-in-class 3B) and Llama 3.2 3B (enterprise ecosystem) for HR departments.

item.title: Global SLM Domain-Specific Applications Analysis
item.description: Analysis of representative SLM use cases replacing LLMs across healthcare, finance, legal, education, and HR. SLM market reaching $5.45B by 2032 (CAGR 28.7%), comparing 8 models including Phi-4, Gemma 3n, and Qwen3.

item.title: Expert Systems with Applications — In-Depth Journal Analysis
item.description: In-depth analysis of ESWA, the world's largest AI applications journal. IF 7.5 (WoS) / 10.48 (Scopus), h-index 290, 1,385 articles/year. Covers 13.8-month review delays and submission strategy.

item.title: OpenClaw vs Competitors: Personal AI Agent Comparative Analysis
item.description: Comparative analysis of personal AI agents centered on OpenClaw (200K+ GitHub Stars), Manus (Meta's $2B acquisition), NanoClaw, and Omi. Examines the security crisis and market growth trajectory ($52.6B by 2030).

item.title: Global Skill Ontology Ecosystem: Major Provider Comparative Analysis
item.description: Comparative analysis of skill taxonomy and ontology providers including Lightcast (33,000+ skills), Pearson/Credly, LinkedIn Skills Graph (39,000 skills), O*NET, ESCO, and Eightfold AI.

item.title: Fujitsu "Takane" and AI-Driven Development Platform: Full Lifecycle Automation Impact
item.description: Fujitsu achieves full lifecycle automation from requirements to integration testing using its proprietary LLM "Takane" and 4-layer multi-agent architecture. 100x productivity demonstrated (3 person-months to 4 hours) in the $24B AI coding market (2030).

item.title: ACM TORS Deep Analysis: The Birth and Impact of the First Dedicated Recommender Systems Journal
item.description: Birth of the world's first dedicated recommender systems journal ACM TORS, LLM4RecSys special issue, 18-member editorial board analysis, and competing journal comparison. Recommendation engine market projected to reach $33.2B by 2030.

item.title: Top 5 Global Authorities in Recommender Systems
item.description: In-depth analysis of five global authorities (Konstan, He, Koren, Tang, McAuley) who shaped modern recommender systems, from collaborative filtering to GNN-based recommendations.

item.title: Moltbot/OpenClaw: The Rise of Personal AI Agents and the Security Crisis
item.description: Analysis of OpenClaw's explosive growth with 183K GitHub stars and the security crisis from 42,000+ exposed control panels across 82 countries.

item.title: Hugging Face: The Dominant Force in Open-Source AI Platforms
item.description: The "GitHub" of AI with 2M models. Analysis of Transformers v5, LeRobot robotics, smolagents framework, and $130M ARR growth strategy.

item.title: Microsoft Purview and Agent Services Analysis
item.description: Comprehensive analysis of data governance and autonomous agents in the AI era. Detailed comparison of Unified Catalog, Foundry Agent Service, Microsoft Agent Framework, and Copilot Agents.

item.title: The End of SaaS and the Transformation from LMS to LXP and HCMS
item.description: As AI agents disrupt SaaS per-seat pricing, learning management evolves from LMS to LXP and HR management transforms into HCMS. The LXP market surges to $28.9B by 2033 (CAGR 33.79%).

item.title: NVIDIA Datacenter GPU Deep Dive: H100, H200, B200, GB200
item.description: Deep analysis of GPUs actually used in AI research. From H100 (80GB HBM3) to H200 (141GB HBM3e, 45% faster), B200 (192GB, 8TB/s), and GB200 NVL72 (1.44 ExaFLOPS). Also covers Meta's 350K and xAI's 100K GPU arms race.

item.title: NVIDIA Blackwell & RTX 50 Series Deep Dive
item.description: 92% market share dominance. Complete analysis from RTX 5090 (21,760 cores, 32GB GDDR7, $1,999) to B200/GB200 data center GPUs and 2026 Rubin architecture.

item.title: DGL (Deep Graph Library) Deep Dive: Rapid GNN Market Growth
item.description: GNN market projected to grow from $320M in 2024 to $1.65B by 2030 at 31.2% CAGR. Deep analysis of DGL 2.0 GraphBolt's 56% memory reduction, NVIDIA cuGraph integration, and DGL-LifeSci drug discovery applications.
